cycle_position.summary: Repriced and settled: after two years of upward drift, single-tenant net lease caps have found their level (Boulder Group avg 6.80%, down 1 bp QoQ; Marcus & Millichap 2025 mean 6.5% was a 12-year high). Strong bifurcation: necessity retail (grocery, pharmacy, discount) tight; discretionary/power-center carries the risk premium. Grocery-anchored national average ~6.7%, stack ~5.5% (Publix/Trader Joe's institutional) to ~7.1% (discount-anchored); Class A primary 5.75-6.50%.

supply_demand.value: Effectively no new strip/neighborhood retail supply for a decade in most East Coast metros — existing centers hold pricing power.

debt_terms.value: NNN with credit tenants finances at 65-75% LTV non-recourse at the larger tickets; small single-tenant deals are local-bank recourse.

small_investor_verdict.entry_vehicle: One single-tenant NNN asset ($1-2M buys a QSR/auto-parts/dollar-store box at 6.2-6.8%) or a small unanchored strip in a secondary metro.
small_investor_verdict.reasoning: The passive counterweight to the hands-on multifamily core: bond-like income, zero rent regulation, minimal management. The trade-offs are flat growth (fixed bumps), binary tenant-credit risk on single-tenant boxes, and dark-box re-leasing risk. For THIS buyer it's a diversification slot, not the main event — the value-add skill set adds nothing to a 20-year Mister Car Wash lease.

gaps: East Coast strip-center comps at the $1-2M ticket
Mall tier: excluded as inaccessible/secularly challenged at this budget
